rv.q: Resolutely honest and brilliant, this is a lionhearted revelation in dramatic form.
This is a play about someone embracing their past to move forward to who they are.
Shamiso intimately and scathingly reveals the lazy cruelties of the bureaucratic systems which fail to extend empathy or understanding.
"No ID" becomes something brisk, revealing, sometimes amusing, and above all self-accepting.
The insight into the process of alteration – the way he has had to raise himself as a man – is riveting.
Shamiso's story is undeniably an important one to tell. But there shouldn't be an artistic trade off to do so.
Tatenda Shamiso makes it unequivocally clear with No I.D. that he is a creative force to be reckoned with, and a performer more than worthy of his accolades.

cn.t: Critics praise Shamiso's hopeful, self-accepting one-man show about his transgender journey, celebrating its honesty, humor, and joy amid bureaucratic struggles, though one reviewer questions whether it meets Royal Court standards.
